title: Scalar endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional simple algebra module
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], meaning that every nonconstant polynomial over $K$ has a root in $K$. Let $A$ be a unital associative $K$-algebra: a unital associative ring with a unital homomorphism $K\to Z(A)$ into its centre. Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] with a unital left $A$-module structure whose action satisfies $(ca)v=c(av)$ for $c\in K$, $a\in A$, $v\in V$, where the action of $K\subseteq A$ agrees with the given scalar multiplication. Assume that the only $A$-stable $K$-subspaces of $V$ are $0$ and $V$. Write $\operatorname{End}_A(V)$ for the ring of additive maps $f:V\to V$ satisfying $f(av)=af(v)$ for all $a,v$, with pointwise addition and composition. Then the homomorphism $K\to\operatorname{End}_A(V)$, $c\mapsto(v\mapsto cv)$, is bijective; equivalently every such $f$ is multiplication by a unique scalar in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 14.1, printed p.280, first sentence of the continuation of the proof: for a simple module over an algebraically closed field, End_A(V)=k (cf. Proposition 4.20).
